title: Equality schemes for sections of a coproduct of fppf sheaves
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], fix its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $I$ be a small set in that convention. Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $C=\coprod_iG_i$ be their coproduct in sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and write $c_i:G_i\to C$ for the coprojections. For a scheme $X$ over $S$, write $h_X(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,X)$. Let $T$ be a site object, let $a,b\in C(T)$, and let $T=\coprod_iA_i=\coprod_iB_i$ be their clopen partitions, with component sections $a_i\in G_i(A_i)$, $b_i\in G_i(B_i)$ satisfying $c_i(a_i)=a|_{A_i}$ and $c_i(b_i)=b|_{B_i}$. Here a clopen partition is a pairwise disjoint open covering, with its open subscheme structures [def-weil-open-immersion]; empty pieces are allowed. Set $D_i=A_i\cap B_i$. Suppose each sheaf on schemes over $D_i$ given by $Z\mapsto\{f:Z\to D_i\mid f^*(a_i|_{D_i})=f^*(b_i|_{D_i})\}$ is represented by a scheme $E_i\to D_i$ (representability as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]). Then the scheme coproduct $E=\coprod_iE_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with its induced map to $T$, represents the equality sheaf of $a$ and $b$: for every $S$-scheme $Z$ in the site there is a bijection $$\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,E)\ \cong\ \{f:Z\to T\mid f^*a=f^*b\},$$ natural in $Z$ and compatible with projection to $\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,T)$. Equivalently $h_E\simeq h_T\times_{C\times C}C$, where $h_T\to C\times C$ is $(a,b)$ and $C\to C\times C$ is the diagonal. The isomorphism on the summand $E_i$ is induced by its given equality of component sections. No algebraic-space hypothesis on the $G_i$ is assumed.

proof.text: For the given coproduct L of E_i, retain only indices K for which E_i has a point. Choosing a point and mapping it into the pairwise disjoint D_i injects K into the underlying set of T, so K is small in the scheme universe. Form its scheme coproduct using lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family. Empty schemes are initial, so reinserting the omitted indices preserves the coproduct universal property. Colimit uniqueness identifies this coproduct with L, proving that the given j_i are open immersions and jointly cover L.

proof.text: Extract from each given local cartesian square that p_i is monic, the two component sections pull back equally along p_i, and every map into D_i with equal component restrictions lifts to E_i. Naturality of c_i and MapsTo give equality of a and b after restricting along j_i. The open cover of L by the j_i is an fppf cover; separatedness of C gives q*a=q*b.

proof.text: For f:Z to T with f*a=f*b, apply lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition to pull back the supplied A and B partitions. Uniqueness identifies these partitions, so each open Z_i maps to D_i. Naturality of the coprojections identifies the images of the restricted component sections, and sectionwise injectivity gives equality in G_i. The local cartesian square yields a lift v_i:Z_i to E_i. The scheme coproduct property of Z_i provided by the partition theorem lifts to Over S because its forgetful functor creates colimits. Descend the maps v_i followed by j_i to g:Z to L. Colimit extensionality and the specified equation j_i q=p_i inclusion give gq=f.

proof.text: If fq=gq for two maps Z to L, pull back the A partition along fq using lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition. On the piece Z_i, both maps land in the range of j_i: a covering summand j_k over a point of A_i must have k=i by disjointness of the A pieces. The universal property of open immersions gives factorizations of both restricted maps through E_i. Since p_i and D_i to T are monic, j_i q is monic and these factorizations agree. The scheme coproduct extensionality on the Z_i gives f=g; hence q is monic.

proof.text: Test the displayed square at every object of the presheaf category. The equality q*a=q*b proves commutativity. Monicity of q proves injectivity of the map to compatible pairs. A compatible pair (s,f) satisfies s=f*a=f*b; the lift constructed above supplies its preimage, with first coordinate s by functoriality. The pointwise pullback criterion yields IsPullback for the original arrows. All arguments allow empty pieces and empty index types.
